test_title: PYST 51: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which practice demonstrates judicious energy use at home?

options.text: Keeping all appliances on standby mode

solution:
The correct answer is __**Using bulbs or fluorescent tubes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Judicious energy use** involves the **efficient** and **responsible** consumption of **electricity** and other resources to minimize waste and reduce the **environmental impact**.
 
• **Using bulbs or fluorescent tubes** for illumination is a standard and necessary practice; however, choosing **Fluorescent tubes** or **CFLs** over traditional **incandescent bulbs** is a mark of **energy efficiency** as they consume significantly less **wattage** for the same amount of light. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Keeping appliances on **standby mode** contributes to **"vampire power"** or **phantom load**, where devices continue to draw **electricity** even when not in active use. This leads to **cumulative energy waste** over time. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Heating an empty room** continuously represents a total loss of **thermal energy**, as the heat generated does not benefit any occupant. This practice increases **utility costs** and **carbon footprints** unnecessarily. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Overusing air-conditioners**, especially at very low **temperature** settings or when not needed, places an extreme **load** on the **power grid** and consumes high amounts of **electrical energy** due to the **compressor's** operation. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Energy Conservation Act, 2001:**

 
 
• In **India**, this **Act** provides the legal framework for **energy efficiency** and conservation.
 
• It led to the establishment of the **Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE)**, which regulates energy standards for appliances.
 
 
 
• **BEE Star Rating System:**
 
 
• The **Star Labeling** program was launched in **2006** to help consumers identify **energy-efficient** appliances.
 
• Appliances like **Refrigerators**, **Air Conditioners**, and **Geysers** are rated from **1 to 5 stars**; a **5-star** rating indicates the highest **energy savings**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Lighting:**
 
 
• **Incandescent Bulbs:** Convert only about **10%** of energy into light, while **90%** is wasted as **heat**.
 
• **Fluorescent Tubes/CFLs:** Use about **75%** less energy than incandescent bulbs and last much longer.
 
• **LED (Light Emitting Diode):** The most **modern** and **judicious** choice, offering the highest **durability** and lowest **energy consumption**.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG):**
 
 
• **Goal 7** aims to ensure **affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy** for all by the **year 2030**.
 
• Practicing **judicious energy use** at **home** directly contributes to reducing **Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions** and combating **Climate Change**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tips for Energy Saving:**

 
 
• Always switch off **lights** and **fans** when leaving a room to ensure **zero wastage**.
 
• Use **natural sunlight** during the day to reduce the **dependency** on **artificial lighting**.
 
• Regular maintenance of **electrical appliances** improves their **operational efficiency** and reduces **power consumption**.
